title: Prospective analysis of preoperative heart rate variability and psychophysiological stress parameters as biomarkers for postoperative delirium and neurocognitive disorders in cardiac surgery patients
summary:
Background: After heart surgery, patients can sometimes experience confusion (POD) or cognitive impairments (POCD). These conditions can significantly reduce quality of life and even increase the risk of illness or death. However, it is difficult to determine beforehand which patients are at higher risk. The aim of this study is to investigate whether certain measures, such as heart rate variability (HRV) and stress factors before the surgery, can predict whether a patient will develop POD or POCD after surgery.

Method: The study will involve 240 patients undergoing planned heart surgery using a heart-lung machine at the Kerckhoff Clinic in Bad Nauheim. One day before the surgery, various tests will be conducted: the patients' cognitive abilities, their perceived stress levels, their physical stress (through a saliva sample), and their heart rate variability will be measured. After the surgery, both in the intensive care unit and later on the regular ward, patients will be checked for signs of confusion (POD). Upon discharge and again three months after the surgery, further tests will assess whether there are any cognitive impairments (POCD).

Discussion: If we can determine certain preoperative measures like HRV and stress as warning signs, we could better identify at-risk patients. This could lead to the development of treatments that help prepare high-risk patients before surgery and prevent problems after surgery.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting (CABG)
-Aortic Valve Replacement (AVR)
-Sufficiently good knowledge of the German language, as the neuropsychological tests are language-dependent.
-Capable of giving informed consent
-Written consent from
Exclusion criteria:
-Preoperative psychiatric and neurological conditions (dementia, depression, stroke) with acute symptoms that could affect neuropsychological testing
-Re-operation
-Emergency surgery
-Pacemaker
-Acute medical treatment for a heart-related condition within the last 3 months (stent, TAVI, heart attack, myocarditis…)
